thread.title_full: Panic as nearly 30 students assessed after pepper spray released inside LA high school - NewsBreak

author: Peter Rubinstein
title: Panic as nearly 30 students assessed after pepper spray released inside LA high school - NewsBreak
text:
By Peter Rubinstein ,
1 hours ago More than two dozen students at a Los Angeles high school on Wednesday were forced into lockdown and assessed by fire officials after pepper spray was released in a classroom.
A student at Panorama High School in Panorama City reportedly used a can of pepper spray in a classroom full of students, according to the Los Angeles Unified School District. The Los Angeles Fire Department and its HazMat team responded to reports of five students complaining of throat pain and dizziness , creating a triage area on the school campus.
Officials assessed about 28 patients for minor symptoms, such as throat irritation and headaches, as they sheltered in place in their classroom, the fire department said. Fourteen students were deemed to be in good condition, and were released to their families. The remaining students were unaffected.

"All patients are in good/fair/stable condition and there is no ongoing threat," the fire department said in a chemical investigation bulletin. "All HazMat readings are at normal background levels."
"The unaffected students were released via normal procedures without incident. No transports were required. No injuries reported to LAFD personnel. No further updates anticipated," the department wrote in a follow-up bulletin.
Aerial footage from local media showed a grouping of LAFD ambulances and fire trucks during the brief campus lockdown.
An LAUSD spokesperson issued a statement following the incident.
"This is the Principal with an important announcement. The health and safety of our students and our staff remains my top priority," they said, according to ABC7 .
"I wanted to take the time to inform you of an incident where school staff intervened when a student used a canister of pepper spray inside a classroom. We have notified the parents of the students involved and are investigating the incident further in accordance with Los Angeles Unified policy," the statement continued.

"Out of an abundance of caution, the campus was placed on a brief lockdown at approximately 3:25 pm while Los Angeles School Police officers investigated further. All students not affected or exposed are being released with a modified dismissal," the statement read.
The spokesperson said the school district is providing counselors to students who require support or someone to speak to about the Wednesday incident, and encouraged parents to contact them if they felt their child needs assistance.
"This incident provides an opportunity to speak with your child about making positive choices and to remind them to tell an adult if they are experiencing issues with other students. We also encourage everyone to follow the District's message: if you see something, say something," the spokesperson said.
